entry.dc:title: TRUCKS VERSUS HIGH-ANGLE CONVEYOR HAULAGE IN OPEN PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Frizzell E.
entry.dc:description: Under contract with the U. S. Bureau of Mines, Dravo Corp. made a study to evaluate the technical and economic feasibility of using a high-angle conveyor system as an alternative to truck haulage in metal and non-metal open pit mining. Such a system includes an in-pit mobile crusher. In order to determine performance specifications, four copper mines, two taconite mines, two phosphate mines and one gold mine were inspected.

entry.dc:title: ENERGY SAVING IDEAS FOR OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Rixen W.
entry.dc:description: The use of semi-mobile crushing plants in open pit mines makes a combination of trucks and conveyors economical and energy efficient.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING AT SYNCRUDE OIL SANDS PLANT.
entry.dc:creator: Regensburg B.
entry.dc:description: The article describes construction and operation of the Mildred Lake operation of Syncrude Canada Ltd. in Alberta.

entry.dc:title: OPODEPE MOLY PROSPECT: DISCOVERY AND EXPLORATION.
entry.dc:creator: Ordonez G.
entry.dc:description: Opodepe is located in the state of Sonora. There is preliminary evidence of molybdenum mineralization in such quantities so as to suggest a possible large scale open pit mining operation.

entry.dc:title: OXIDE AND SULPHIDE COPPER MINING AT TONG LU SHAN.
entry.dc:creator: Argall G.
entry.dc:description: 4,000 tons per day of copper ore are mined using underground and open pit mining methods. Twelve ore bodies have been identified, seven are producing, and exploration is currently underway.

entry.dc:title: Practical experience with centrifugal pumps in mine dewatering application.
entry.dc:creator: Kosyna G.
entry.dc:description: This paper shows typical installations of dewatering pumps in underground and open pit mining and gives a brief introduction to mine dewatering problems. Environmental conditions as well as the urgency of cost reduction of mine dewatering systems impose design objectives on pumps for mine dewatering. (English abstract)

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING. PART 3. QUARRYING AND GENERAL STUDIES (CITATIONS FROM THE ENGINEERING INDEX DATA BASE).
entry.dc:description: Worldwide research dealing primarily with methods, equipment, and explosives used in drilling, blasting, and open pit mining is cited. Topic areas cover air blast and ground vibration, open pit equipment selection and maintenance, slope stability, and optimization of open pit mining using computerized simulation techniques. This updated bibliography was prepared by searching the 1970-November 1979 data base of Engineering Index. It contains 219 abstracts, 40 of which are new entries to the previous edition.

entry.dc:title: MINING IN THE NEXT DECADE.
entry.dc:creator: Kostuik J.
entry.dc:description: The author identifies 13 major highlights of the industry over the last 10 years. He discusses current trends in mining techniques, open pit mining, underground mining and ocean mining.

entry.dc:title: IMPACT OF MINING ACTIVITIES ON WATER QUALITY IN WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA
entry.dc:creator: Duda A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Jawra Journal of the American Water Resources Association
entry.dc:description: ABSTRACT: An intensive water quality investigation was conducted in western North Carolina to determine whether water quality problems existed from point and nonpoint source inputs of sediment from surface mining activities. Depth integrated measurements of sediment transport and biological sampling of benthic communities indicated that very serious water quality problems were caused by erosion from a concentrated area of open pit mining for mica, kaolin, and feldspar. The erosion occurred on haul roads, active mines, inactive mines, and tailings disposal piles. The need for using specific “Best Management Practices” for erosion control on the mining operation is discussed. These practices need to be implemented to restore populations of trout to the degraded reaches of the river. Additional monitoring data are presented that indicate that the biological integrity of surface waters can be preserved in the vicinity of point source mining discharges when the operators utilize proper practices in settling and neutralizing their effluent. While much has been done to abate the point source discharges, attention now needs to be focused on the nonpoint sources of sediment from mining operations. Copyright © 1980, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved
entry.authkeywords: aquatic biology | mining erosion | nonpoint source pollution | sediment transport | water quality monitoring

entry.dc:title: On the theoretical accuracy of photogrammetric volume determination.
entry.dc:creator: Jacobi O.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Archives of Photogrammetry Vol 23 Part B4 Commission IV
entry.dc:description: Photogrammetric methods are used in volume estimations for open pit mining in the mining industry, and for volume estimation of water reservoirs in irrigation works. Height values of a set of terrain points or contour lines are determined by photogrammetric strip and block triangulation and from these the volume enclosed by the terrain surface and a reference level is estimated. There are two error sources in this volume determination, namely photogrammetric triangulation and the terrain roughness. The influence of the photogrammetric triangulation on volume estimation is studied. -from ITC Bibliography

entry.dc:title: LARGE-DIAMETER BLAST HOLE DRILLS.
entry.dc:creator: Nelmark J.
entry.dc:description: Rotary drilling has become effective as an open pit mining tool for blast holes from 6 through 17 one-half -in. diam. Rotary drills are adaptable to drill in clays, soft shales and limestone, and unconsolidated sediments. Production and cost estimates for representative coal, copper and taconite applications are given.

entry.dc:title: New and newsworthy. Hydraulic shovel
entry.dc:description: It is claimed that the RH300 is the biggest and most powerful hydraulic shovel in the world. It was developed by O & K to meet the demand for large capacity, high performance open pit mining machines to remove overburden and to extract underlying minerals and ores. The features of the hydraulic shovel are described. (from paper)

entry.dc:title: ANALYSIS OF EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR ANTHRACITE OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Manula C.V.
entry.dc:description: The Mineral Engineering Department of The Pennsylvania State University has developed a suite of computer models for anthracite open pit mining. Individual subsystems have been developed to (a) interpolate geologic field data to obtain coal tonnages, waste volumes, and strip ratios; (b) simulate equipment performance on selected pit profiles to generate data required to choose coal and waste removal equipment; and (c) evaluate selected cost factors to determine either a rate of return for a specified selling price or vice-versa. This paper describes the application of two of these subsystems, namely the Reserves Model (GEOL) and the Open Pit Materials Handlng Simulator (OPMHS), and how these may be applied for the selection of equipment for a prime anthracite mining site.

entry.dc:title: Increase of water temperature and its effect upon a power plant cooling pond
entry.dc:creator: Gerking E.
entry.dc:description: For over 20 years a lake created by open pit mining has served as a cooling water resource for the brown coal power plant at Wolfersheim in Upper Hesse and has been the recipient for the recycled heated water. Cooling towers are non-existant. The impact upon temperature dispersion, chemical balance and ecology within the lake is a substantial part of the report. Recommendations are given to adapt adequate regulations in future water management.

entry.dc:title: Luzenac's Talc.
entry.dc:creator: Py L.
entry.dc:description: France's Societe des Talcs de Luzenac is mining a major talc deposit in the Pyrenees at an altitude of 1800 meters. This article provides some interesting information about the company's mining operation, describing the key features of open pit mining, the aerial cableway and the ore cleaning.

entry.dc:title: OIL MINING, FINAL REPORT ON TASK 014, 1979.
entry.dc:creator: Reed W.F.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
entry.dc:description: This ESCOE task report covers the production of oil by open pit mining of oil sand deposits in the United States and surface extraction of the oil. A companion area is application of the same technology to shallow oil fields in lieu of other means of enhanced oil recovery. The report surveys possible mineable domestic sites and suggests candidates for developmental projects. Possible extraction techniques including those used in Canada, solvent extraction and retorting are discussed. It is pointed out that separation of fines and recovery of solvent are the two major extraction problems. The report points out that ability to comply with environmental requirements placed on mining and process operations will be a major factor slowing development; another will be the problems in leasing Federal lands. A review of cost ranges is also presented. There is a discussion of the one United States project now in the engineering stage together with a prediction of possible future development and production levels. The report includes recommendations as to government actions to bring the technology on stream. These include tax credits and research aimed at developing relatively small (10,000 barrels-a-day or less) extraction plants to fit the U. S. sites.

entry.dc:title: How to protect the natural environment - possibilities and limits
entry.dc:creator: Zepter K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The open pit mining of deposits undoubtedly means an encroachment on the natural environment, which, in contrary to other industrial projects, does not permit to turn to other locations for reasons of environmental conservation. In view of this the enterprises do their utmost to minimize the environmental effects of quarrying and processing of raw materials. Examples are provided to show, that with the planning of mining, after the last exploitation of a deposit, preparatory steps are to be taken in order to achieve subsequent use of the location.

entry.dc:title: ASPECTS OF DEVELOPMENTS OF THE COAL INDUSTRY IN THE SINGLETON-MUSWELLBROOK AREA, NEW SOUTH WALES.
entry.dc:creator: Lauder R.
entry.dc:description: Coal resources of 45 thousand million tonnes of which 15 thousand million tonnes lie at a depth of less than 200 m have been estimated. The area is destined to become the largest coal producing area in New South Wales. Coal is being won by strip mining, open pit mining and by underground means. The techniques involved are described. Production of both coking coal and steaming coal is expected to rise within the next 25 years.

entry.dc:title: SYNCRUDE BEATS TAR SANDS, COLD WITH MODIFIED EQUIPMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Watson L.
entry.dc:description: The 7000 acre mine site, located on lease NO. 17 in the Athabasca tar sands, represents the largest and most comprehensive open pit mining operation ever attempted. The mining equipment is described.

entry.dc:title: GIANT MINE AND MACHINERY MAKE HISTORY.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: In 1978, the German lignite mining company, Rheinische Braunkohlenwerke AG, (Rheinbraun), started work on what will become the world's biggest open pit mining operation near Hambach. Over the next 50 years, the company will extract 2. 5 billion tons of lignite from 300-foot-thick seams, working to a depth of 1200 feet below the surface.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS (BWE).
entry.dc:creator: Benecke K.
entry.dc:description: Nearly all excavators, such as shovels, draglines, wheel loaders, scrapers, have only one digging tool, so that all parts of a working cycle have to be performed separately and consecutively. This intermittent cycle operation distinguishes them from the bucket wheel excavator. The development of open pit mining equipment for higher capacities described here was favoured by geological conditions of West German lignite deposits. Despite its low thermal value, lignite has become the cheapest raw material for power generation.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING AND MAINTENANCE AT THE CLIMAX MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Brown C.
entry.dc:description: The Climax mine is located 120 km west of Denver Colo. on the Continental Divide at Fremont Pass. Production is divided between the underground operation, providing 27,000 mtpd and the open pit, providing 16,000 mtpd. Open pit mining in the high Rockies, with a major underground mine immediately below, causes many problems that tax the ingenuity of the underground, the open pit and plant engineering staffs.

entry.dc:title: OFF-HIGHWAY BRAKE PERFORMANCE DIFFICULT TO PREDICT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: New and more stringent codes are evolving for the braking performance of off-highway open pit mining trucks. A series of actual truck performance tests was conducted to learn whether stopping performance was predictable, to determine fade characteristics of available linings, and to compare actual with theoretical brake performance under various conditions. Tests were carried out with a 152 tonne (170 ton) WABCO Haulpak truck equipped with Rockwell Stopmaster shoe brakes. A series of stops at maximum brake operating pressures were run on level, 6%, and 10% grades, empty, half loaded, and fully loaded. Two different lining mixes were studied.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT EQUIPMENT: GIANT DOZERS, LARGEST CRAWLER MOUNTED ELECTRIC SHOVEL.
entry.dc:creator: Kennedy B.
entry.dc:description: Equipment developments for open pit mining in 1977 were generally aimed at improving the performance and productivily of existing equipment lines. The uncertainty of the world economy and its effect on the mining industry has evidently not provided much incentive for extensive development of new equipment. Some companies, however, did introduce new products.

entry.dc:title: Technological Measures for Environmental Protection in the Planning and Operation of Open Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Lechner E.
entry.dc:description: Measures for reducing the acoustic and dust emissions from open pit mining are reviewed, as well as measures for planning stone quarries so as to cause the minimum amount of environmental damage, and measures for the reclamation of disused open fit mining areas.
